report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 5 of daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py: _promote_one, promote_candidates, _promote_locked, _governance_verdict, run_write_wave. Verified docstring claims against code.
risks: promote_candidates | high | 'Never raises' claim broken: function may raise RuntimeError if ledger_path is None and resolve_spine_db_path returns an error but the error branch returns early, but the function body as written has no bare raise; however, _PromotionLock could raise PromotionUnavailable (caught), but other exceptions from lock acquisition are not caught. | Check if _PromotionLock.__enter__ can raise other exceptions not caught.

run_write_wave | medium | 'NEVER writes the primary checkout' claim relies on scheduler.dispatch for non-write tasks; if dispatch writes to primary checkout, claim broken. | Verify scheduler.dispatch behavior.

run_write_wave | medium | 'Returns one result dict per entry in tasks, position-matched' claim depends on scheduler.dispatch returning results in same order; the code assumes this but does not verify. | Confirm scheduler.dispatch contract.
run_write_wave | low | 'cancel=None is byte-identical to behaviour before cancel existed' is uncheckable in this chunk; no prior version code present. | Cross-reference earlier version.

handoff.purpose: Contains _promote_one, promote_candidates, _promote_locked, _governance_verdict, and run_write_wave functions with their docstrings and implementation.

symbols.name: _promote_one
symbols.note: Wrapper around _promote_one_inner with catch-all exception handling.

symbols.name: promote_candidates
symbols.note: Phase 2: promotes gated candidates in order, never raises.

symbols.name: _promote_locked
symbols.note: Internal function that creates integration worktree and iterates candidates.

symbols.name: run_write_wave
symbols.note: Executes write-mode tasks through gated path, never promotes or writes primary checkout.

claims.text: Never raises: every failure mode (lock unavailable, apply refused, cumulative gate failed, base moved and the retry also failed) is a refusal in the returned report, not an exception.
claims.why: The function catches PromotionUnavailable and returns a report, but other exceptions from _PromotionLock (e.g., TimeoutExpired if not subclass of PromotionUnavailable) are not caught; also, the code may raise RuntimeError if ledger_path is None and resolve_spine_db_path returns an error but the error branch returns early, but that is caught. However, the main risk is from _PromotionLock itself. The docstring claims never raises, but the implementation does not catch all exceptions from the lock acquisition.

claims.text: ``cancel`` is forwarded to every STALENESS-triggered regeneration (``_reattempt``'s own ``TaskAttempt``) AND to the cumulative re-gate's own ``command_gate`` call inside ``_promote_one_inner``
claims.why: The forwarding to _reattempt and command_gate occurs inside _promote_one_inner, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: the SAME unconditional ``git reset --hard``/``clean -fd`` that already runs for a genuine cumulative-gate failure also runs for a cancelled one
claims.why: The reset logic is in _promote_one_inner, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Filtered by object IDENTITY, not dataclass equality: two distinct candidates can legitimately compare equal on fields.
claims.why: Line 905: live_ids = {id(c) for c in live} uses id() for identity.

claims.text: ``_governance_verdict`` never re-derived here. That function's own docstring is explicit that a SECOND opinion on ``promotion_allowed`` is how an override sneaks in
claims.why: The docstring references get_governance's docstring, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Any failure to even ASK the question -- ``daedalus.core`` unimportable, the call itself raising -- reports the vocabulary's ``unknown``, not a silent True.
claims.why: Lines 1001-1006: catches ImportError and general Exception, returns state='unknown'.

claims.text: ``unknown`` and ``absent`` stay distinct facts (see ``daedalus.core.GOVERNANCE_STATES``): this only ever manufactures ``unknown`` for a failure that happened HERE; a real ``absent`` receipt is already reported correctly by ``get_governance`` itself and passes through unchanged.
claims.why: The distinction between 'unknown' and 'absent' depends on get_governance's implementation, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``cancel``, when given, is forwarded to ``gate_candidates`` for every concurrent attempt in this wave.
claims.why: The call to gate_candidates is not in this chunk; this function does not call gate_candidates directly.

claims.text: A caller driving a longer-lived loop ... can pass one shared token/``KillSwitch`` here so a stop request reaches every in-flight ``TaskAttempt`` and every in-flight cumulative gate this wave started, cooperatively, instead of relying solely on the killswitch's process-wide sweep
claims.why: The forwarding of cancel to TaskAttempt and cumulative gate happens inside gate_candidates and _promote_one_inner, not in this chunk.

claims.text: ``assignments`` MUST be ``scheduler.accept(tasks, repo_root=repo_root)``'s own return, in the SAME order as ``tasks``
claims.why: Line 1033: if len(assignments) != len(tasks): raise RuntimeError enforces length match; order is assumed but not explicitly checked.

claims.text: Returns one result dict per entry in ``tasks``, position-matched
claims.why: Lines 1047-1050: results list initialized with None for n tasks; write_idx and other_idx fill results positions accordingly.

claims.text: Non-write tasks in the SAME wave (advisory, or bounced to the senior lane) are NOT touched by the gated path: they are delegated back to ``scheduler.dispatch``, scoped to just their own indices
claims.why: Lines 1042-1050: other_idx tasks are dispatched via scheduler.dispatch and results placed at correct indices.

claims.text: NEVER writes the primary checkout and never calls ``promote_candidates``.
claims.why: No call to promote_candidates in this chunk; no git commands on primary checkout.

claims.text: Legacy ``auto_promote`` values are reported as denied input and coerced to ``"never"``.
claims.why: Lines 1038-1039: if auto_promote not in AUTO_PROMOTE_LEVELS: auto_promote = 'never'. However, there is no reporting of the denial; the docstring says 'reported as denied input' but the code silently coerces. This may be a broken claim if 'reported' means logged or returned.

observations.what: promote_candidates docstring claims 'Never raises' but the code may raise from _PromotionLock if lock acquisition fails with an exception not caught.
run_write_wave docstring claims legacy auto_promote values are 'reported as denied input', but the code silently coerces to 'never' without any logging or error.
The claim that cancel is forwarded to gate_candidates and _promote_one_inner is uncheckable; the actual forwarding is not in this chunk.
